cites.quote: API tests use Vitest and Supertest against a throwaway PostgreSQL 16 with a fixed clock.

Web tests use
Vitest with jsdom and Testing Library.
Every PRD requirement has at least one test whose name starts with its ID
status = 'NO_SHOW' AND starts_at >= period start AND starts_at < end of today
link `/appointments` with query status NO_SHOW, from period.from and to period.to
The selected period is one of `Today`, Last 7 days or Last 30 days.
DSH-7: the period is Today, Last 7 days or Last 30 days, default Today
A `No-show` is a past appointment the patient did not attend.
the exact totals assertion (C10) gains noShows, plus a case with a No-show inside and one outside the period
The No-show cases live in `api/test/dashboard-no-shows.test.ts`, a file with its own database:

findings.suggested_fix: Keep the new file, but flag the change from the design for the impl step. Or move the cases back into dashboard.test.ts with isolated setup.
findings.text: The design puts the new No-show inside/outside cases in the existing API dashboard test. The plan moves them to a new file, api/test/dashboard-no-shows.test.ts. The plan gives a reason, but this differs from the design and the test layout has no such file.

rubric_items.reason: All 10 acceptance criteria have a test: S-1 AC1-AC5, S-2 AC1-AC2 and S-3 AC1-AC3. REQ-1 to REQ-10 are traced. With TP-12 dropped, no test points to a criterion that does not exist.
Counts, bounds and list matching are tested at API integration level. The tile title, link, reload and zero value are tested at web unit level. There are no e2e or manual tests.

The changed endpoint's new field has a lower-boundary test (TP-3), an upper-boundary test (TP-14), a zero edge case (TP-13) and a period regression (TP-15). No test asserts behaviour that the inputs do not state.
Uses the strategy's tools: Vitest, Supertest, fixed clock, jsdom and Testing Library. Uses the existing test files from the layout, and test names start with requirement IDs as the strategy requires.
Titles are specific and can be run as written. Each title starts with its requirement ID. TP-14 explains how the clock is set. The gap where TP-12 was is explained in resolves and Scope.
